steps.tx: Diagnostic **ST-segment elevation** requires new elevation at the J-point in two **contiguous leads** of at least **1** mm in all leads except V2-V3, where thresholds are at least **2.5** mm in men under **40**, at least **2.0** mm in men **40** and older, and at least **1.5** mm in women. These age- and sex-adjusted cutoffs prevent overdiagnosis of benign early repolarization while ensuring timely identification of acute transmural infarction.
steps.say: Diagnostic ST-segment elevation requires new elevation at the J-point in two contiguous leads of at least 1 mm in all leads except V2-V3. In leads V2 and V3, the elevation threshold is at least 2 point 5 mm in men under 40, at least 2 point 0 mm in men 40 and older, and at least 1 point 5 mm in women. These age- and sex-adjusted cutoffs prevent overdiagnosis of benign early repolarization while ensuring timely identification of acute transmural infarction.

steps.tx: The 12 lead tracing shows **ST segment elevation** at the J point in **contiguous leads** across the anterior chest with a broad **hyperacute T wave**. The magnified V2 and V3 complexes make the early takeoff and tall peaked wave easy to see. Recognizing this pattern matters because it marks acute transmural infarction that needs rapid reperfusion assessment rather than dismissal as benign early repolarization.
steps.say: This tracing shows an anterior ST elevation heart attack. The ST segment lifts off the J point in neighboring chest leads, especially V2 and V3, and the T wave looks tall and peaked. Spotting these changes matters because they signal a sudden blocked artery. Rapid recognition leads to fast reopening of the vessel and more saved heart muscle.

vis.alt: A 12 lead ECG shows ST elevation at the J point in neighboring anterior leads with a tall hyperacute T wave magnified over leads V2 and V3.
vis.caption: Anterior ECG showing J point elevation with hyperacute T waves Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Primary percutaneous coronary intervention** is the preferred **reperfusion strategy** if it can be performed within **120** minutes of STEMI diagnosis. Establishing immediate wire crossing restores antegrade epicardial coronary flow and improves myocardial salvage, significantly lowering recurrent reinfarction, intracranial hemorrhage, and mortality compared with pharmacological fibrinolytic therapy.
steps.say: Primary percutaneous coronary intervention is the preferred reperfusion strategy if it can be performed within 120 minutes of STEMI diagnosis. Establishing immediate wire crossing restores antegrade epicardial coronary flow and improves myocardial salvage, significantly lowering recurrent reinfarction, intracranial hemorrhage, and mortality compared with pharmacological fibrinolytic therapy.

nodes.label: Can Primary PCI Be Done Within 120 Minutes?
YES: Immediate Transfer for Primary PCI (Door-to-Balloon < 90 min)
NO: Administer IV Fibrinolytic Bolus Within 10 Minutes

steps.tx: If PPCI cannot be achieved within **120** minutes, intravenous **fibrinolytic therapy** with **tenecteplase** must be administered within **10** minutes of STEMI diagnosis, followed by transfer for pharmacoinvasive assessment. Routine coronary angiography is subsequently performed within **2** to **24** hours after successful lysis, whereas failed reperfusion mandates immediate rescue PCI.
steps.say: If PPCI cannot be achieved within 120 minutes, intravenous fibrinolytic therapy with tenecteplase must be administered within 10 minutes of STEMI diagnosis, followed by transfer for pharmacoinvasive assessment. Routine coronary angiography is subsequently performed within 2 to 24 hours after successful lysis, whereas failed reperfusion mandates immediate rescue PCI.

steps.tx: **Posterior myocardial infarction** is diagnosed by ST depression at least **0.5** mm in leads V1-V3 with tall R waves and upright T waves, confirmed by ST elevation at least 0.5 mm in posterior **leads V7-V9**. True posterior wall ischemia arises from left circumflex or distal right coronary occlusion, presenting as mirror-image ST elevation on standard precordial leads.
steps.say: Posterior myocardial infarction is diagnosed by ST depression at least 0 point 5 mm in leads V1-V3 with tall R waves and upright T waves, confirmed by ST elevation at least 0 point 5 mm in posterior leads V7-V9. True posterior wall ischemia arises from left circumflex or distal right coronary occlusion, presenting as mirror-image ST elevation on standard precordial leads.

left.title: Anterior Leads V1-V3 Mirror Signs
points: Horizontal or downsloping ST depression >= 0.5 mm
Tall, broad R waves with R/S ratio > 1 in lead V2
Represents electrical mirror image of posterior wall

right.title: Posterior Leads V7-V9 Direct Signs
points: Lead V7 at posterior axillary line 5th space
Lead V8 at mid-scapular line 5th space
Lead V9 at left paraspinal border 5th space

steps.tx: **Right ventricular infarction** complicating inferior STEMI is identified by ST-segment elevation at least **1** mm in right-sided **lead V4R**, presenting with hypotension, clear lung fields, and elevated jugular venous pressure. Preload maintenance with intravenous saline is paramount; nitrates and diuretics are strictly avoided because they precipitate catastrophic right ventricular failure.
steps.say: Right ventricular infarction complicating inferior STEMI is identified by ST-segment elevation at least 1 mm in right-sided lead V4R, presenting with hypotension, clear lung fields, and elevated jugular venous pressure. Preload maintenance with intravenous saline is paramount; nitrates and diuretics are strictly avoided because they precipitate catastrophic right ventricular failure.

nodes.label: Inferior STEMI with Hypotension and Elevated JVP
Obtain Right Precordial ECG: Check Lead V4R
Confirm ST-Segment Elevation >= 1 mm in Lead V4R
Administer IV Saline & Strictly Withhold Nitrates/Diuretics

steps.tx: The right sided set pairs inferior ST elevation in leads two, three and aVF with STE in **lead V4R**, the marker of **right ventricular infarction**. The inset reminds that these patients are **preload dependent** with hypotension yet clear lungs, because the failing right chamber cannot fill the left. That physiology is why fluids support output while nitrates and diuretics would collapse it.
steps.say: Start with the bottom rhythm strip and the inferior leads, which lift off the baseline as an inferior attack. Then move rightward to V4R, where the same lift confirms the right ventricle is involved. Those patients need filling, not unloading, so the box pairs clear lungs and low pressure with fluids over nitrates. Use V4R as the branch point that flips the usual acute coronary management.

vis.alt: Right sided ECG shows inferior ST elevation with confirmatory ST elevation in lead V4R.
vis.caption: Right sided ECG tracing linking inferior elevation to V4R right ventricular involvement, Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Modified **Sgarbossa criteria** identify acute coronary occlusion in the presence of left bundle branch block or ventricular pacing: **concordant ST elevation** at least **1** mm, concordant ST depression at least 1 mm in V1-V3, or excessively discordant ST/S ratio at most **-0.25**. The Smith modification replacing absolute 5 mm discordance with the proportional ratio greatly enhances diagnostic accuracy.

The Smith modification replacing absolute 5 mm discordance with the proportional ratio greatly enhances diagnostic accuracy.

rows: ≥  1 mm in leads with positive QRS
≥  1 mm in precordial leads V1, V2, or V3
ST/S ratio ≤  -0.25 in excessively discordant leads
Replaces older absolute 5 mm discordance rule

steps.tx: **Prasugrel** given as a **60** mg loading dose followed by **10** mg daily or **ticagrelor** given as a **180** mg loading dose followed by **90** mg twice daily is recommended over clopidogrel in primary PCI. Potent P2Y12 inhibition achieves rapid platelet suppression, significantly reducing ischemic recurrent infarctions and acute stent thrombosis.
steps.say: Prasugrel given as a 60 mg loading dose followed by 10 mg daily or ticagrelor given as a 180 mg loading dose followed by 90 mg twice daily is recommended over clopidogrel in primary PCI. Potent P2Y12 inhibition achieves rapid platelet suppression, significantly reducing ischemic recurrent infarctions and acute stent thrombosis.

left.title: Prasugrel Regimen
points: Loading dose 60 mg, maintenance 10 mg once daily
Dose reduction to 5 mg if weight < 60 kg or age >= 75
Contraindicated in prior stroke or TIA

right.title: Ticagrelor Regimen
points: Loading dose 180 mg, maintenance 90 mg twice daily
No dose reduction required for elderly or low body weight
Safe in patients with prior ischemic cerebrovascular disease

steps.tx: **Complete revascularization** of non-infarct-related culprit arteries in hemodynamically stable STEMI multivessel disease reduces major adverse cardiac events as shown in the landmark **COMPLETE trial**. Staged or index procedure PCI of non-culprit lesions with significant stenosis lowers cardiovascular death and recurrent infarction compared with culprit-only PCI.

nodes.label: STEMI Patient with Multivessel Coronary Disease Undergoing PPCI
Successful Primary PCI of Culprit Infarct-Related Artery
